title: Bulgogi Rice Bowl
subtitle: Korean sweet-soy beef bowl. 10 min prep + 20 min marinate, 6 min cook.

ingredients.thai_market_tip: Ask Tops/Villa butcher for shabu-shabu cut — already thin. Or freeze 20 min and slice 3mm.
Asian pear at Tops fresh aisle. Fuji apple is the easy sub — same job (enzymes that tenderise + sweetness). Korean cooks grate it on a microplane straight into the marinade.

ingredients.note: Oil cap — this is your tsp. In the marinade.

ingredients.thai_market_tip: Tops Korean aisle. The bright-red flakes — not Thai chili flakes, which are hotter and darker.

ingredients.note: Quick stovetop blanch then squeeze dry — adds fibre + colour.

substitutions.note: Becomes dak bulgogi. Marinate the same, cook 4 min/side.
Low-carb mode. Tops frozen cauliflower rice packs, 90 sec microwave.

steps.text: Whisk grated pear, soy, honey, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, gochugaru — this is the bulgogi marinade.
Add sliced beef. Massage marinade in 1 min. Cover, fridge 20 min (or up to overnight).
Heat non-stick pan SCREAMING hot, no oil. Add beef in one layer — don't crowd. Sear 60–90 sec per side.
Push beef to one side, crack eggs into the empty space. Fry hard — crispy edges, runny yolk.
Microwave rice packs per label (~90 sec each).
Build bowls: rice base, spinach + kimchi to one side, beef on top, fried egg crowning. Sesame seeds, spring onion.

notes: The grated pear is the move — the actinidin enzyme breaks beef proteins down chemically, faster than salt. 20 min marinate gives the same tender bite as 4 hours of plain soy. Don't add oil to the pan; the beef has enough. The egg yolk is the sauce that ties everything together.
